content_units: Ontario Key Deposit: What Matters Here

In Ontario, a key deposit is generally only allowed to cover the replacement cost of keys, fobs, or entry devices, and it should be returned when the keys are given back. A   CAD 1,200   key deposit is often far above actual replacement cost, so this is the main issue to focus on.
Dates from your situation
- Lease ended:   2025-08-31
- Keys returned:   2025-08-31
- Forwarding address sent:   2025-09-01
- Landlord stopped responding:   2025-09-10
Practical Ontario Checklist and Next Steps
1) Gather the core documents
Keep everything in one folder, in date order if possible.
- Lease agreement or tenancy agreement
- Receipt, lease clause, or e-transfer record showing the   CAD 1,200   key deposit
- Proof keys were returned on   2025-08-31
- Email sending your forwarding address on   2025-09-01
- Any replies from the landlord before they stopped responding
- Screenshots of texts, emails, call logs, or messages showing follow-up attempts
- Move-out inspection notes, if any
- Photos of returned keys/fobs, key handoff, dropbox, or building office return process
- Proof of your new mailing address
- Bank records showing no repayment was received
2) Build a simple timeline
Prepare a one-page summary with:
- Date tenancy ended
- Date keys were returned
- Date forwarding address was provided
- Date(s) you asked for repayment
- Date landlord stopped responding
This helps if you later speak with a clinic, tenant duty counsel, or file an application.
3) Send one clear written repayment request
Use email first, and if you have a mailing address, also send it by trackable mail. Ask for payment by a short fixed deadline.
What to include:
- The amount:   CAD 1,200
- The fact that keys were returned on   2025-08-31
- The fact your forwarding address was provided on   2025-09-01
- A short request for repayment by e-transfer or cheque
- A reasonable deadline, such as   7 calendar days
- A calm note that if unpaid, you may consider next available remedies
4) Preserve proof of the demand
After sending the message:
- Save the sent email as PDF
- Screenshot the sent message and timestamp
- Keep postal receipt/tracking if mailed
- Note whether the landlord opens, replies, or ignores it
5) If there is still no response, consider the Landlord and Tenant Board route

For general information, the next practical escalation is usually to review whether a   Tenant Application about Money the Landlord Owes (T1)   fits your situation. This is commonly used where a tenant says the landlord collected or kept money unlawfully.
Bring:
- Your lease
- Deposit proof
- Key return proof
- Forwarding address proof
- Communication history
- Your timeline
6) Get free or low-cost Ontario tenant guidance before filing
Helpful support options:
- Local community legal clinic
- Tenant Duty Counsel / legal aid resources
- CLEO self-help materials
- Tribunals Ontario / Landlord and Tenant Board forms and instructions
7) Keep the issue narrow and practical
For a non-courtroom, general-information approach, your strongest practical points are:
- Key deposits in Ontario are generally limited to actual replacement cost
- Keys were returned
- The landlord has not refunded the deposit
- You gave a forwarding address and followed up
Repayment Options at a Glance
Step   What to do   What to include   Best outcome
1   Organize records   Lease; deposit proof; key return proof; emails; timeline   You have a clean evidence package
2   Send final written request   Amount; dates; payment method; 7-day deadline   Landlord repays voluntarily
3   Send by second channel   Email plus trackable mail if possible   Better proof landlord received demand
4   Get tenant guidance   Legal clinic; CLEO; LTB information   Confirm best form/process
5   Consider LTB money application   Copies of all documents and timeline   Formal route to seek repayment
Concise Draft Message Requesting Repayment
Subject: Return of key deposit – [Rental Address]
Hello [Landlord Name],

I am following up regarding the   CAD 1,200 key deposit   for [rental address]. My tenancy ended on   2025-08-31  , and I returned the keys the same day. I also provided my forwarding address by email on   2025-09-01  .
Please return the   CAD 1,200   key deposit within   7 calendar days   of this message by e-transfer to [your email] or by cheque mailed to [your mailing address].
If you believe any amount is being withheld for key replacement, please provide a written explanation and itemized documentation showing the actual replacement cost.
Thank you,
[Your Name]
[Phone]
[Email]
